summary: Léon Rodet was an Indologist and historian who studied at the École Polytechnique from around 1851 to 1853. He served as a member of the Société Asiatique from approximately 1865 to 1895.

Sinologist and philosopher Léon Vandermeersch studied at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held posts at Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and served as Director of the EFEO (1989–1993).

Léonard Eugène Aurousseau worked in sinology and history/archaeology, studying under Édouard Chavannes at EPHE and INALCO (~1908–1911). He joined the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 1909, teaching history, archaeology, and Chinese, and served as its Director from 1926 to 1929.

Lê Mạnh Thát worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history/archaeology. He earned a BA from the University of Saigon (~1961–1965) and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1974), later holding a post at Vạn Hạnh University (~1974–1975).

M. A. Mehendale was an Indologist and linguist who served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955). He held long-standing professorial posts in Sanskrit and Vedic Literature at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Historian and Indologist M. Athar Ali studied at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1947 to 1953. He subsequently worked as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from approximately 1953 to 1995.
Indologist M. Christopher Byrski studied under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He served as Head of the Indology Department at the University of Warsaw (attested 1991).

Indologist and linguist M. D. Balasubrahmanyam completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he also held a post (attested 1967). He served as Reader at Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha and Principal at Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan (attested 1973).

M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian who studied at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and UCL under Ernest Arthur Gardner and others. He served as Professor of History, department head, and arts dean at the University of Mysore.

Philosopher M. M. McCabe studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She was a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990) and Professor at King's College London (1990–2014), also holding posts at UCL and Newnham College.

M. R. Raghava Varier works in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, later serving as Professor at the University of Calicut.

M. S. A. Rao was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (~1949–1953) and at the University of Delhi. He held a post at the University of Delhi (~1955–1985), Syracuse, and Pennsylvania.

Indologist and archaeologist M. S. Nagaraja Rao studied under M. N. Deshpande at Mysore and Pune. He worked at Karnatak University and Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1984–1987).

M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1899), and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University (attested 1899).
Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar M. Shinoda studied at Agoura High School (~1991–1995) and the Art Center College of Design (~1995–1998), having also studied under Seiren Matsunami.

M. Victor Stanley worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Lawrence University, University of Wisconsin-Madison, University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as Supervising-Principal for the Corona-Norco Unified School District.

M. Yamunacharya worked in philosophy and Indology, studying under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

Scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati studied at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities. She served as Associate Professor and Asian Studies Director at CSU Sacramento (2002–2016), with posts at the Asian Art Museum and elsewhere.

Maalyada Konduparti works in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at Andhra University (2015), Alliance University (2016–2017), and REVA University (2017–2021), and became an Associate Professor at GITAM University in 2021.
Maanasa Visweswaran is an Indology and computational studies researcher who studied and held a post as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
